prompt: Walk me through your background in two minutes and end with why forward deployed work.
signals: A story that ends at this role, not a résumé read-out
Evidence of building things real users depend on
Fits in two minutes
follow_up: What part of your current job would you miss?

prompt: What do you think a forward deployed engineer does day to day?
signals: Building and customer work in the same week
Ownership through to production and adoption
Realism about travel, ambiguity and context switching
follow_up: Which part of that do you expect to find hardest?

prompt: Why work on customers' problems rather than on a product team?
signals: A real preference backed by past choices
Understands the trade: less depth in one codebase, more range
No disdain for product engineering
follow_up: When have you enjoyed customer-facing work the most?

prompt: Tell me about a system you built that real users depend on today.
signals: Specific users and what they rely on
Your part, stated plainly
What it took to keep it running
follow_up: What broke in its first month?

prompt: How do you feel about travel and working on site with customers?
signals: An honest answer with any limits stated up front
Understands why on-site time matters
No over-promising
follow_up: What would make on-site work hard for you?

prompt: Which languages and tools are you productive in on day one?
signals: Honest depth versus familiarity
Python plus one systems or web stack is common
How fast you pick up a customer's stack
follow_up: Tell me about the last stack you had to learn under pressure.

prompt: What is the most ambiguous project you have taken on?
signals: How you created structure
Who you talked to first
What you shipped and how you knew it worked
follow_up: What would you do differently?

prompt: How do you keep up with changes in models and AI tooling?
signals: A concrete habit, not a list of newsletters
Learning by building and measuring
Healthy skepticism of announcements
follow_up: What changed your mind recently?

prompt: Describe a time you explained a technical decision to a non-technical executive.
signals: Started from their goal, not the technology
Gave a clear recommendation and its cost
Checked understanding
follow_up: What did they push back on?

prompt: What kind of customer problem would you not want to work on?
signals: A considered answer with a reason
Self-awareness
Not a list of everything you dislike
follow_up: Have you ever worked on one anyway?

prompt: Where do you want to be in three years?
signals: A direction connected to this role
Open to how the role grows
Not a title chase
follow_up: What would make this role a step toward that?

prompt: What questions do you have for us?
signals: Questions about customers, scope of ownership and how success is measured
Shows research
Asks about the team you would join
follow_up: What would make you turn down an offer from us?

prompt: A logistics customer says: 'We want an AI agent for dispatch.' Where do you start?
signals: Separates the requested solution from the problem
Asks about the workflow, volumes and the cost of errors
Ends with a small, testable first step
follow_up: What would make you advise against an agent here?

prompt: A bank wants AI to cut the time it takes to answer customer complaints. Structure the problem.
signals: Maps the complaint workflow and where time goes
Separates waiting time from work time
Names regulatory constraints early
follow_up: Which step would you automate first, and which never?

prompt: A hospital group wants an assistant that drafts replies to patient messages. What do you need to know before proposing anything?
signals: Clinical risk and who approves each reply
Message volumes, types and current turnaround
Data handling and where the system may run
follow_up: Which message types stay out of scope in phase one?

prompt: The customer's VP wants a demo in two weeks and production in six. How do you scope it?
signals: Separates a demo from a production system out loud
Proposes a narrow slice that can really ship
States what must be true by week six
follow_up: What do you say if the VP rejects your slice?

prompt: A manufacturer wants AI to predict machine failures. They have three years of sensor data and no failure labels. What do you propose?
signals: Finds the labels: maintenance logs, work orders, operators
Questions whether prediction is the real need
Plans a baseline before any model
follow_up: How would you know the model is better than the current maintenance schedule?

prompt: An insurer's claims team says the AI pilot 'isn't accurate enough.' How do you find out what that means?
signals: Asks for examples and builds a labelled set
Splits error types by business cost
Agrees what 'enough' means as a number
follow_up: What if the team cannot agree on the right answers?

prompt: The customer wants the AI to issue refunds automatically. What is your recommendation?
signals: Separates recommending from executing
Limits, approvals and audit before autonomy
A path to more autonomy based on evidence
follow_up: What evidence would justify raising the automatic limit?

prompt: How would you estimate whether this use case is worth building at all?
signals: Baseline volume, time and cost today
A defensible range for the improvement, not a promise
Cost to build and run, and a break-even view
follow_up: Which of your inputs is the weakest?

prompt: The customer has 40,000 internal documents in five systems and wants a chatbot over all of it. How do you phase it?
signals: Starts from user questions, not from the corpus
One system and one team first
Access control and freshness from day one
follow_up: How do you choose the first system?

prompt: Which success metric would you agree with the customer for a ticket-triage pilot, and what baseline do you need?
signals: A metric tied to the business outcome
A measured baseline over the same period
Guardrail metrics alongside the target
follow_up: What would you do if the baseline does not exist?

prompt: The customer's data cannot leave their network. What changes in your plan?
signals: Model hosting options and their trade-offs
Who operates it and how updates happen
Evaluation without exporting data
follow_up: What capability do you lose, and how do you tell them?

prompt: Two departments want different things from the same pilot. How do you handle it?
signals: Finds the decision owner
Makes the trade-off explicit in writing
Sequences instead of splitting the effort
follow_up: What if the sponsor refuses to choose?

prompt: In week two you find that the process the customer described is not the process people follow. What do you do?
signals: Treats it as evidence, not embarrassment
Updates the plan and tells the sponsor early
Revisits success metrics and scope
follow_up: How do you raise it without blaming the customer?

prompt: Estimate the monthly model cost for an assistant used by 400 agents, 20 requests each per working day.
signals: States assumptions for tokens and price
Shows the arithmetic
Names the levers that change the answer most
follow_up: How would caching or a smaller model change it?

prompt: The customer asks: 'Why can't we just buy a chatbot product?' How do you answer?
signals: Takes the question seriously
Compares on their requirements, not on taste
Recommends buying when buying fits
follow_up: When would you tell them to buy?

prompt: What would make you recommend that the customer not use AI for this problem?
signals: Deterministic rules already solve it
Errors are too costly with no review step
No data or no owner
follow_up: Have you ever made that recommendation?

prompt: How do you decide what goes in phase one and what waits?
signals: Value, risk and dependency, made explicit
Something real ships in phase one
Deferred items are written down with a reason
follow_up: What is the most common thing teams wrongly put in phase one?

prompt: The pilot hit its metric but the frontline team does not use it. Diagnose.
signals: Talks to users and watches them work
Checks workflow fit, trust and incentives
Measures adoption, not only accuracy
follow_up: What would you change first?

prompt: Build a service that answers questions from these documents, with citations. You have 60 minutes.
signals: Gets a thin end-to-end path working early
Decides when to abstain in code
Tests on a handful of known questions before polishing
follow_up: What would you build in the next 60 minutes?

prompt: Clean this customer export and report the median resolution time by priority.
signals: Inspects the data before writing code
Writes down assumptions to confirm with the customer
Fails loudly on values it does not recognize
follow_up: Which assumption would change the answer most?

prompt: Build an agent that handles order tickets with these four tools. What do you build first?
signals: The loop with a step budget and parsing
Policy checks in code before side effects
Escalation that reaches a human
follow_up: How do you test it without a real model?

prompt: How would you make this prototype safe to show the customer's leadership tomorrow?
signals: Narrows the demo to what works
Guards against the known bad inputs
Prepares a fallback and says what is not ready
follow_up: What do you never do in a live demo?

prompt: Retrieval returns the right document but the answer is wrong. What do you check?
signals: Chunking and what context the model actually saw
Prompt and instruction conflicts
Whether the answer needs reasoning across passages
follow_up: How would you turn this into a regression test?

prompt: Write a client for this paginated, rate-limited API.
signals: Pagination until the cursor ends
Retry-After and backoff
Token refresh and idempotent writes
follow_up: Which call is the dangerous one to retry?

prompt: How would you test an LLM-backed function in CI?
signals: Deterministic tests around the model call
A small labelled set with thresholds
Recorded responses or a fake for unit tests
follow_up: How do you stop flaky tests from being ignored?

prompt: You have 20 minutes left and two features unfinished. What do you do?
signals: Says it out loud and picks one
Leaves the code runnable
Explains what is missing and how it would be done
follow_up: How do you decide which one?

prompt: Add structured output to this extraction step and handle malformed responses.
signals: Schema validation, not string matching
A bounded retry with the error fed back
A safe failure path when retries run out
follow_up: What do you log when validation fails?

prompt: How would you let the customer's team change prompts without breaking production?
signals: Prompts versioned like code
An eval gate before release
Rollback in minutes
follow_up: Who should own the eval set?

prompt: How would you log this agent so the customer's audit team can follow a decision?
signals: Every tool call with inputs, outputs and the policy result
Correlation by ticket or request id
Personal data masked or excluded
follow_up: How long would you keep these logs?

prompt: Parse 300 PDF invoices into a table. What is your plan for the first hour?
signals: Looks at a sample first and groups layouts
Builds an extraction check on a few hand-labelled invoices
Plans for the ones that will not parse
follow_up: What accuracy would you report, and how?

prompt: Answers were fine last week and are wrong today. Nothing in our code changed. Where do you look?
signals: Data, model version and configuration changes
Reproduces with a known question
Compares against a saved good run
follow_up: How do you make this faster to diagnose next time?

prompt: A user from one tenant saw another tenant's data in an answer. Walk me through your first hour.
signals: Treats it as a security incident first
Contains: disable or scope the path
Finds the leak path: retrieval filter, cache key, logs
follow_up: What do you tell the customer, and when?

prompt: Latency doubled after the customer added 10,000 documents. Diagnose.
signals: Measures where the time goes
Checks index, retrieval size and context length
Fixes the cause, not only adds hardware
follow_up: What would you monitor from now on?

prompt: The agent loops, calling the same tool again and again. Likely causes and fixes?
signals: Tool results not reaching the model, or ignored
No stopping condition or budget
A tool error the model cannot recover from
follow_up: Where do you enforce the budget?

prompt: The nightly sync sometimes misses records. How do you find out why?
signals: Pagination and cursor handling
Time zones and update windows
Retries that skip instead of repeat
follow_up: How would you prove the fix?

prompt: The model's JSON output fails to parse 3 percent of the time. What do you do?
signals: Collects the failures and looks at them
Schema-constrained output if available
Retry with the error, then a safe fallback
follow_up: Is 3 percent acceptable? When?

prompt: Model costs tripled overnight. How do you investigate?
signals: Usage by route, tenant and prompt version
Retries and loops
A cap or alert to stop the bleeding
follow_up: What guardrail would have caught this?

prompt: An integration works in the test tenant and fails in production with 401s after about an hour. Why?
signals: Token expiry without refresh
Different credential or scope in production
Clock skew
follow_up: How would you test for this before go-live?

prompt: Here is a failing test and a 200-line module. Talk me through how you debug it.
signals: Reads the failure message and the test first
Narrows with prints or a debugger, one hypothesis at a time
Explains the fix and adds a test
follow_up: What if you cannot reproduce it locally?

prompt: The customer says the bot made something up. How do you reproduce and fix it?
signals: Gets the exact input, time and user
Checks what context the model saw
Adds the case to the eval set before fixing
follow_up: How do you explain the fix to the customer?

prompt: Design an assistant for a bank's complaint handlers, deployed inside the bank's own cloud.
signals: Requirements and constraints first
Data flow with trust boundaries
Evaluation, human review and audit
follow_up: What changes if the bank needs answers in two languages?

prompt: Design document Q&A over 2 million pages with access controls that mirror the source systems.
signals: Permission-aware retrieval, checked at query time
Incremental indexing
Citations and freshness
follow_up: What happens when permissions change in the source system?

prompt: Design an agent that can take actions in a customer's ERP system.
signals: Tool layer with policy checks and limits
Human approval for high-impact actions
Idempotency and audit
follow_up: How do you test it without touching production?

prompt: How do you design for a customer whose data must stay in one country?
signals: Region-pinned storage, processing and logs
Model hosting options in region
Proof for the auditors
follow_up: What about backups and support access?

prompt: Design the evaluation and release process for a customer-facing assistant.
signals: A labelled set by slice
Gates in CI with thresholds
Monitoring and rollback after release
follow_up: Who signs off on a release?

prompt: Design a system that drafts replies to patient messages for clinicians to approve.
signals: Clinician approval on every reply
Triage of urgent messages out of the AI path
Logging and review of edits
follow_up: How would you measure whether it saves clinicians time?

prompt: How would you serve a model inside a customer's network with no internet access?
signals: Model artifacts, serving and updates offline
Capacity planning on their hardware
Monitoring that stays inside
follow_up: How do you ship an update?

prompt: Design the multi-tenant architecture for a platform your company deploys to 30 customers.
signals: Isolation model and where tenant id is enforced
Per-tenant configuration and evals
Noisy-neighbor and cost controls
follow_up: When would one customer need a dedicated deployment?

prompt: How do you handle prompt injection in a system that reads customer emails?
signals: Treats email content as untrusted data
Limits what the model can do with it
Detection and review, not only prompt wording
follow_up: What is the worst action this system could be tricked into?

prompt: Design human review for an AI that classifies insurance claims.
signals: Confidence and risk-based routing
Reviewer tooling and feedback capture
Sampling of auto-approved items
follow_up: How do you know reviewers are not rubber-stamping?

prompt: How would you serve 200 requests per second at peak with a 2-second latency budget?
signals: Latency budget per stage
Caching, batching and smaller models where possible
Load tests and graceful degradation
follow_up: What gets dropped first under overload?

prompt: What would you put in a security review package for the customer's CISO?
signals: Data flow diagram and data inventory
Threat model including prompt injection
Controls, logging and incident response
follow_up: Which question do CISOs ask that engineers forget?

prompt: Design monitoring for an AI assistant after go-live.
signals: Quality signals, not only uptime
Cost and latency per route
Alerts with owners and runbooks
follow_up: How do you sample conversations for review?

prompt: How do you hand the system over to the customer's team when you leave?
signals: Runbooks, evals and dashboards they can operate
Training and a shadow period
Clear support boundaries
follow_up: How do you know the handover worked?

prompt: Design retrieval for documents that change every hour.
signals: Change capture and incremental updates
Versioning and deletion
Freshness shown to the user
follow_up: What happens to cached answers?

prompt: Where would you put guardrails in an agent that can send emails on a user's behalf?
signals: Draft by default, send with approval
Recipient and content checks in code
Rate limits and audit
follow_up: When would you allow sending without approval?

prompt: Tell me about a time you owned a problem end to end.
signals: Clear ownership beyond your assigned part
Actions you personally took
A measurable or observable result
follow_up: What did you hand off, and to whom?

prompt: Tell me about a time a customer was unhappy with your work.
signals: Owns the part that was yours
Listened before fixing
What changed afterward
follow_up: How did the relationship end up?

prompt: Tell me about a time you pushed back on a customer request.
signals: The reason was the customer's interest
Offered an alternative
Kept the relationship
follow_up: What would have happened if you had agreed?

prompt: Tell me about a time you shipped something under a hard deadline.
signals: What you cut and why
How quality was protected
What you did after the deadline
follow_up: Would you make the same cuts again?

prompt: Tell me about a mistake you made in production.
signals: States the mistake plainly
Containment and communication
The prevention you put in place
follow_up: Who did you tell first?

prompt: Tell me about a time you had to learn a new domain fast.
signals: A method for learning
Who you learned from
How you checked your understanding
follow_up: What did you get wrong at first?

prompt: Tell me about a time you disagreed with your manager or product team.
signals: Disagreed with evidence, not volume
Committed once decided
Outcome and what you learned
follow_up: What if you had been overruled?

prompt: Tell me about a time you worked with very little direction.
signals: Created structure
Checked in at the right moments
Delivered something usable
follow_up: How did you decide what mattered?

prompt: Tell me about a time you had to say no to a senior stakeholder.
signals: The no protected something real
Said with a reason and an alternative
Trust afterward
follow_up: How did you prepare for the conversation?

prompt: Tell me about a time you turned field feedback into a product change.
signals: Saw a pattern across customers
Made the case with evidence
Followed through to release
follow_up: What did the product team push back on?

prompt: Tell me about the hardest technical problem you solved at a customer site.
signals: Constraints you could not change
How you narrowed the cause
What you left behind for the customer
follow_up: What would you do differently?

prompt: Tell me about a time you were wrong about a technical decision.
signals: Owns it without excuses
How you found out
How you corrected course
follow_up: How do you test your decisions now?

prompt: Tell me about a time you had to deliver bad news.
signals: Early, not late
Facts, impact and a plan
Took questions
follow_up: How did they react?

prompt: Tell me about a time you simplified something complex for a customer.
signals: Started from what they needed to decide
Removed detail without hiding risk
Checked understanding
follow_up: What did you leave out?

prompt: Tell me about a time you had to balance speed and quality.
signals: Named the trade-off explicitly
Protected what could not be undone
Paid back the shortcut
follow_up: Where do you never cut corners?

prompt: Tell me about a time you built trust with a skeptical team.
signals: Understood why they were skeptical
Small wins they could verify
Gave them control
follow_up: How long did it take?

prompt: Tell me about a time you handled conflicting priorities across two customers.
signals: Made the conflict visible
Used impact to decide
Communicated with both
follow_up: Who decided in the end?

prompt: Tell me about a time you went beyond your role to unblock a project.
signals: The blocker and why it mattered
What you did that was outside your job
Did not create a new problem
follow_up: Would you do it again?

prompt: Tell me about a project that failed. What did you learn?
signals: A real failure, not a disguised success
Your part in it
A lesson you have applied since
follow_up: What early signal did you miss?

prompt: Tell me about a time you protected a customer from a risk they did not see.
signals: Spotted the risk
Raised it in a way they could act on
The outcome
follow_up: What if they had ignored you?

prompt: Tell me about a time you documented or handed over work so others could run it.
signals: What they needed to operate it
How you tested the handover
What happened after you left
follow_up: What did they still call you about?

prompt: Why do you want to leave your current job?
signals: Pulled toward this role, not only pushed
No complaints about people
Consistent with your story
follow_up: What would make you stay?

prompt: I'm the customer's CTO. Your demo failed in front of my board yesterday. Explain.
signals: Owns it without excuses
Explains cause in plain words
Concrete plan and a date
follow_up: What do you promise, and what do you not?

prompt: I'm the head of operations. My team doesn't trust the AI. Convince me to keep the pilot.
signals: Asks what happened before arguing
Offers changes that give the team control
Agrees a fair test with a deadline
follow_up: What if the team is right?

prompt: I'm the CISO. Tell me why I should let your system read our email.
signals: Starts from the data flow
Specific controls, not reassurance
Offers a narrower first scope
follow_up: What would you not ask me to approve?

prompt: I'm the business sponsor. I want the AI to approve claims automatically next month.
signals: Supports the goal
Shows the evidence needed and the risk
Offers a staged path
follow_up: What do you do if I insist?

prompt: I'm a frontline agent. This tool makes my job slower. Respond.
signals: Asks to see how they work
Takes the complaint as data
Commits to a specific follow-up
follow_up: What would you change this week?

prompt: I'm the procurement lead. Why does this cost more than the chatbot we already license?
signals: Compares on outcomes and requirements
Is honest about where the cheaper option is enough
Total cost, not only license
follow_up: What would make you recommend the cheaper option?

prompt: I'm the customer's lead engineer. I think your architecture is overbuilt. Defend it.
signals: Listens for the specific concern
Ties each component to a requirement
Willing to simplify
follow_up: Which component would you remove first?

prompt: I'm the project sponsor. We're cutting the budget in half. What do we drop?
signals: Protects the core outcome
Makes the trade-offs explicit
Asks what the sponsor values most
follow_up: What is the minimum you would still put your name to?

prompt: I'm the data owner. You can't have production data for testing. What now?
signals: Respects the constraint
Proposes alternatives: masked data, synthetic data, testing in their environment
Agrees a path to evidence
follow_up: What risk does that leave?

prompt: Explain to our executive team, in three minutes, what the pilot proved and what it did not.
signals: Leads with the decision they need to make
Separates measured results from hopes
A clear recommendation
follow_up: What number would you put on the first slide?
